entities.rationale: A rich, capable state whose collapse risk is mostly global doom plus a war or trade shock hitting its imported food and energy. Near-free essentials need SI-scale growth, because health spending alone is already near the 10% line.

Nuclear power and food self-sufficiency make it resilient, but weak political stability and rising debt add some risk. Essentials at 27% of income, with high health costs, make abundance unlikely without SI.

Chronic grid failure, severe water stress and very high violence make a five-year loss of electricity, water or security plausible. Low life expectancy and weak state capacity put abundance far out of reach.

Peaceful and rich, but it imports 79% of its energy, carries very high debt, faces growing water stress and has one of the oldest populations, which pushes health costs up. Collapse outside global doom is unlikely.

A third of people are already undernourished, the climate is getting harsher and politics is fragile, so a majority food or security failure is the main path to collapse. Abundance needs SI gains to reach a poor country with life expectancy below 75.
Plentiful water and energy exports are strengths, but armed groups, high homicide and low political stability make security the main pillar at risk. Middle income limits abundance.

War with North Korea, or a regional blockade cutting the 83% of energy it imports and much of its food, is the main risk on top of global doom. Its strong state and tech base help abundance under SI, but extreme aging drags it down without SI.
Peaceful and rich with strong solar, but severe and worsening water stress threatens water and farming. Rapid aging keeps health costs high, which limits abundance.
As a food and energy exporter it is physically secure, but repeated economic crises could degrade health care and incomes. Middle income and macro instability make near-free essentials unlikely.

Abundant energy, water and food, plus strong institutions, leave global doom as nearly its whole collapse risk, along with spillover if the US becomes unstable. Health spending keeps essentials well above 10% unless SI cuts costs sharply.

The war passes five years in early 2027 with strikes nationwide and occupation, so a majority losing security, and repeated attacks on the grid, may already count as collapse. Renewed Russian aggression later is a further risk.
Water depends on desalination, food is mostly imported, and extreme heat, regional war and the end of oil revenue all threaten stability. High military spending also works against near-free security.
It is stable and growing, but as a NATO front-line state next to Russia, war is the main risk beyond global doom. Rapid aging and middling income limit abundance.

As an energy and food exporter with strong institutions it is resilient. The main local risks are drought, heat and a Pacific conflict. Under SI, its wealth and solar resources make abundance comparatively plausible.
Very rich with world-class flood defenses, so the projected 2100 sea-level rise is manageable. Its 88% energy import dependence is the main weak point beyond global doom.

Low debt, clean domestic power, ample water and very effective government leave little collapse risk beyond global doom and a Baltic war. Essentials at 25% of income still need SI-driven cost cuts to fall below 10%.

The richest country here, with hydropower, a huge sovereign fund, the lowest climate vulnerability and essentials already at 20% of income, so it is the likeliest to reach abundance. Food imports and the Arctic border with Russia are minor risks.
